ratings.reviewer_notes: Evaluates clinical efficacy of baricitinib and upadacitinib and separately the IL-6 receptor inhibitor sarilumab; it does not show that either JAK inhibitor modulates IL-6 or interferon signaling.
RA clinical trial establishes baricitinib efficacy but reports no IL-6 or interferon signaling measurements.
In RA fibroblast-like synoviocytes, peficitinib inhibited STAT3 phosphorylation induced by IL-6, IFN-alpha, and IFN-gamma; effects were compared with tofacitinib and baricitinib.
Directly demonstrates that tofacitinib suppresses IFN-alpha production by plasmacytoid dendritic cells and IFN-alpha-driven arthrogenic responses in synovial fibroblasts.

Baricitinib, upadacitinib, and tofacitinib directly inhibited IL-6-, IFN-gamma-, and IFN-alpha-dependent STAT signaling, but experiments used leukocytes from healthy donors rather than an RA population.
Shows in vivo suppression of multiple cytokine-induced JAK-STAT pathways by tofacitinib in RA patients, but the abstract does not explicitly identify IL-6 or interferon among the tested pathways.

RA-focused review directly states that all approved JAK inhibitors suppress IL-6 signaling and identifies interferon suppression by filgotinib, baricitinib, and upadacitinib, with broader cytokine suppression by tofacitinib.
Baricitinib and tofacitinib directly inhibited IFN-alpha-, IFN-gamma-, and IL-6-induced STAT phosphorylation in human immune cells, but the experiments were not performed in RA-derived cells.
General review of tofacitinib clinical utility and JAK biology in RA without specific evidence concerning IL-6 or interferon signaling.
Directly compares filgotinib, upadacitinib, tofacitinib, and baricitinib in healthy and RA blood, showing inhibition of IFN-alpha- and IL-6-dependent STAT signaling.

In RA fibroblast-like synoviocytes, tofacitinib reduced transcriptional markers of myofibroblast differentiation induced by combined IL-6 and TGF-beta, although protein-level confirmation was lacking.

Tofacitinib, baricitinib, and filgotinib inhibited IFN-gamma-induced CEACAM1 expression in healthy-donor neutrophils; the model was motivated by RA but did not use RA patient cells, and IL-6 did not induce the measured response.
